leah.h: FYI nightly evals just flagged a big regression on the long-article-summarize prompt set after onboarding model vX-2026-03. overall pass went 97.8% -> 68.3%, ROUGE-L dropped ~0.22. attaching a tiny repro below.

nightly-bot: [alert] nightly-evals/long-article-summarize: failure-rate up 29.5pp vs baseline (vprev). see /evals/2026-03-20/long-article-summarize/summary.csv

matt.ryan: can you paste a few example inputs + outputs? quick diff helps narrow tokenizer vs weights vs quantization.

leah.h: sample prompt (truncated):
```
Prompt: "Summarize the key arguments in this 1200-word op-ed about urban planning and traffic calming. Focus on tradeoffs, evidence, and one-sentence takeaway."
```
Old model (vprev) output: "The author argues that traffic calming balances safety and throughput, citing randomized crosswalk studies and pilot road diets; tradeoffs include increased local delays but lower severe injuries. Takeaway: prioritize street design that favors vulnerable users while monitoring throughput via pilot metrics."

New model (vX-2026-03) output: "The author argues that traffic calming balances safety and throughput, citing randomized crosswalk studies and pilot road diets; tradeoffs include increased local delays but lower severe injuries. Takeaway: In conclusion, the key point is \"

leah.h: note the new model often ends with a dangling phrase or abruptly stops mid-clause; not just truncation at seq-len, it looks like the decoder produced a reproducible cutoff (same prompt+seed leads to same truncation).

ashok.k: what quantization profile did we ship with the canary? int8->int4 mapping? last canary used q4f16 with group size 128 + fused kernels.

leah.h: we onboarded a weight swap (weights commit: a1f3b9 -> a1f7d2) plus tokenizer updates — new merges file from tokenization repo (bpe merges updated to handle medical tokens). rollout config: canary 10% in nightly cluster, but nightly evals run against canary.

sophia.k: i pulled raw token ids from both tokenizers for the same prompt. old: [1543, 22, 988, 4012,...,2] new: [1543, 22, 988, 4012,...,255,2]. There's an extra token id (255) before EOS in many samples. that smells like a vocab index shift or newline-token mapping changed.

matt.ryan: extra token id before EOS -> could be an inserted special token or off-by-one index after reindexing vocab.json. can you paste the detokenized string including invisible markers?

sophia.k: detokenized (repr): "... lower severe injuries. Takeaway: In conclusion, the key point is \uFFFD\n" — the 0xFF replacement char shows up when our detokenizer sees an unmapped id.

ashok.k: if detokenizer outputs U+FFFD often that strongly suggests the tokenizer vocab ids in the model head don't match the tokenizer we're using at serving time (vocab mismatch). two suspects: 1) tokenizer.json and model's LM head index mapping diverged; 2) quantization pipeline changed indices when folding tokens into embeddings.

leah.h: reproduction steps i used:
```
# local repro (python)
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from model_runner import load_model_local
tok_old = Tokenizer.from_file('tok_vprev.json')
tok_new = Tokenizer.from_file('tok_vx.json')
ids_old = tok_old.encode(prompt).ids
ids_new = tok_new.encode(prompt).ids
print(ids_old[-8:], ids_new[-10:])
model = load_model_local('model_vx-2026-03', quant='q4f16')
out = model.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=60, seed=42)
print(out)
```

leah.h: observed: ids_new contains a 255 before eos token (2). model.generate returns tokens including 255, and detokenizer maps 255->invalid -> U+FFFD in the string.

matt.ryan: good repro. two parallel triage tasks: (A) ashok, check model artifact: confirm embedding matrix size and LM head vocab_size == tokenizer vocab_size at origin commit. (B) sophia, diff tok files (vprev vs vx) for any inserted special token or different token id ordering. i'll bisect the weight commits between a1f3b9..a1f7d2 to see if any conversion script ran.

ashok.k: quick low-effort check: run `python -c "import torch; m=torch.load('model.pth', map_location='cpu'); print(m['lm_head.weight'].shape)"` and compare tok vocab size `len(tok.get_vocab())` — if mismatch, that's it. also check model config tokenizer offset fields.

leah.h: i ran the shape check: lm_head.weight shape (50257, 4096), tokenizer vocab length 50258. off by one.

sophia.k: confirmed: tok_vx.json inserted a new '<sep/>' token at id 255 but the model's lm_head was never rebuilt to include that new token index (conversion pipeline forgot to resize lm_head after merges update).

matt.ryan: aha. that explains the U+FFFD and dangling token (inserted unmapped id then EOS). two fixes: rebuild/retrain LM head (resized embedding + head) or remap tokenizer so new special tokens use unused ids within current vocab size.

leah.h: immediate mitigation: flip canary route off or set rollout fallback to vprev so nightly evals and some customers aren't hit. can anyone flip the canary? @ops-bot we should throttle canary to 0.

ops-bot: acknowledged. commencing canary drain to 0% for model vX-2026-03. will post when complete. :gear:

matt.ryan: medium term: add CI gate in model-onboard job that asserts `len(tokenizer) == lm_head.shape[0]` and fails onboarding artifacts if mismatch. also add a lightweight detokenize sanity test that detokenizes full test prompts and asserts no U+FFFD.

ashok.k: for quantization: verify conversion script preserves lm_head reorder. i suspect q4 conversion script reuses indices and may have masked resize. i'll add a unit test in quant-tooling.

sophia.k: also found ~3 prompts where token boundaries changed (BPE merges different) and that changed content slightly (e.g., "road diets" -> "road di ets" split) which impacted evaluation metrics. separate follow-up: decide if merges change is intended; we may need mapping rules for old promptsets.

leah.h: plan of record: 1) ops drains canary (in flight) 2) matt adds CI gate and starts bisect to find offending conversion commit 3) ashok patches conversion to resize lm_head or we regenerate model artifact with resized head 4) sophia documents tokenizer diff and runs updated tokenization on stable promptset to quantify metric impact 5) we'll re-run nightly evals on a staging cluster with fixed artifacts before re-onboarding.

matt.ryan: assigning myself for bisect, ashok on conversion fix, sophia on token diffs. leah, i'll post a short PR checklist snippet once i have bisect narrowed to candidate commit.

leah.h: thanks all. i'll keep this thread updated; tagging @nightly-bot to re-run smoke after ops finishes drain. :white_check_mark:

nightly-bot: test-run queued: nightly-smoke/repro-vx-token-fix (will run after canary drain).
